title: What's Inside Your Phone? A Journey Into the Heart of a Smartphone 📱
description:
Your smartphone is more powerful than the computers that took humans to the Moon! In this episode we go inside the phone and see how every part works: the processor, memory, battery, screen, camera, antennas and hidden sensors.

00:20 The processor: the brain
01:00 Memory and storage
01:35 The battery
02:15 The screen and touch
03:00 The antennas
03:30 Hidden sensors
04:15 Recap

scenes.text: More powerful than the Moon computers!
scenes.say: The device in your hand is thousands of times more powerful than the computers that took humans to the Moon. So what's actually inside? Let's go in and see.

scenes.caption: The processor: the brain
scenes.say: Let's start with the brain: the processor. A chip about the size of your fingernail that does every calculation your phone needs, from opening apps to running games.

scenes.label: Each one a tiny on-off switch
scenes.say: Inside the processor are billions of tiny switches called transistors. Each one flips on and off billions of times a second, and from those zeros and ones, everything you see is built.

scenes.text: Some transistors are smaller than a virus
scenes.say: These transistors are so small that some are smaller than a virus, visible only under special microscopes.

Next is memory, which comes in two kinds: RAM is super fast and holds the apps you have open, but it's wiped when you turn the phone off. Storage is slower, but it keeps your photos and apps for good.

scenes.caption: Lithium-ion battery
scenes.say: Now the power source: the battery. Most phones use lithium-ion batteries, because they pack a lot of energy into a small, light package.

When you charge, lithium ions move from one side of the battery to the other and get stored there. When you use your phone, the ions flow back, and that movement releases the electricity that runs everything.

scenes.text: Heat is your battery's worst enemy
scenes.say: A quick tip: high heat is your battery's worst enemy. Don't leave your phone in the sun or in a hot car, because it shortens battery life fast.

scenes.caption: The screen: millions of colored dots
scenes.say: Now the screen. It's made of millions of tiny dots called pixels, and each pixel has three even smaller dots: red, green and blue.

scenes.title: How the screen makes every color
items: Each pixel has red, green and blue
Each one glows at a different strength
Your eye blends them into any color
scenes.say: By changing how bright those three colors glow in each pixel, the screen creates millions of colors, and your eye blends them into a complete picture.

right.label: LCD screens
right.sub: One backlight for the whole screen

left.label: OLED screens
left.sub: Each pixel makes its own light

scenes.say: There are two popular types: LCD screens, which use one backlight for the whole screen, and OLED screens, where every pixel lights itself, so black is truly black.

scenes.caption: The touch layer
scenes.say: On top of the screen is a clear touch layer with a fine grid of wires that senses the electric charge in your finger and knows exactly where you touched.
Around the edges of the phone are hidden antennas: one for the cellular network, one for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, and one that picks up signals from GPS satellites.

scenes.title: Hidden sensors always at work
scenes.say: And tiny sensors work nonstop: an accelerometer senses tilt and motion, a gyroscope senses rotation, a proximity sensor turns the screen off when you hold it to your ear, and a light sensor adjusts the brightness for you.

scenes.text: Your step counter uses the motion sensor
scenes.say: Did you know your phone's step counter relies on the motion sensor? It feels the little jolts of every step and counts them.

scenes.title: Recap
items: The battery stores energy in ions
The screen is millions of pixels
Antennas and sensors connect it to the world
scenes.say: So in short: the processor thinks, memory remembers, the battery supplies power, the screen displays, and the antennas and sensors connect your phone to the world around it. All in a device that fits in your pocket.

scenes.say: If you enjoyed the trip, subscribe to How It Works and hit the bell, and tell us in the comments which part of the phone you'd like us to explain in depth.
